Master foot & ankle X-ray interpretation

A structured, case-based trainer for Australian podiatry students — aligned to the Podiatry Board of Australia Professional Capabilities (2022), podiatrist-rebatable MBS imaging items (57521/57523/57527), IWGDF/IDSA 2023 diabetic-foot guidance and the Ottawa ankle/foot rules.

1 · Learn the system

Standard views, weight-bearing vs non-weight-bearing, systematic reading checklist, key angles (HVA, IMA, Meary, calcaneal pitch, Böhler, Gissane), Ottawa rules, podiatrist imaging requests (MBS 57521/57523/57527), ossicle pitfalls, diabetic foot infection vs Charcot.

2 · Work the cases

Real radiographs in a guided flow: presentation → find the abnormality on the film → case questions → write your structured report → compare with the expert report → teaching points and pitfalls.

3 · Test yourself

MCQ bank with spaced repetition and topic mastery, plus a timed OSCE mode (10 questions / 10 minutes) with full review.

4 · Track progress

Per-topic mastery bars, streaks, cases completed, quiz accuracy, items due for review — stored only in this browser.

How podiatrists use X-ray in Australia: registered podiatrists can request Medicare-rebatable plain radiographs of the foot, ankle, leg, femur and knee (MBS items 57521, 57523, 57527). Interpreting those films well is a core graduate capability — this app trains exactly that skill, on real films.

      OSCE history

        References: Podiatry Board of Australia, Professional capabilities for podiatrists (2022) and Accreditation standards: entry-level podiatry programs (2021); MBS note IN.0.6 (items 57521/57523/57527, 55834/55835); Stiell et al., Ottawa ankle rules, JAMA 1993; IWGDF/IDSA 2023 diabetic-foot infection & acute Charcot guidelines; Christman RA, The normal foot and ankle; accessory-ossicle reviews (AJR 2019; SMJ 2018).
        Image sources & licences: all radiographs from Wikimedia Commons — CC0, public domain, CC BY, CC BY-SA — attribution shown per case. Add more by embedding licensed/de-identified images as data URIs with author + licence + source. Never add images with patient identifiers.
